microglial cells can be recruited from the blood and can be induced to differentiate into tumor-supporting cells by glioma-derived factors.
microglia can have both pro- and anti-tumor activities, and that their molecular profile is affected by glioma.
the molecular profile of glioma microglia is characterized by the expression of receptors for glioma-derived factors and the release of molecules that affect the glioma microenvironment.

the development of novel therapeutic approaches for the treatment of glioblastomas, based on the use of microglia as a vehicle for the delivery of therapeutic molecules.
the identification of molecular targets that are involved in microglial functions in glioma.
the development of microglial cell-based therapies for glioma.

microglia are a heterogeneous population of cells, which may have both beneficial and detrimental effects on glioma progression.
microglia are both tumor-supporting and tumor-suppressing.
microglia are multifaceted and can play either a positive or a negative role in glioma.

glioma-derived molecules can modulate microglia functions and that microglia can be used to deliver therapeutic molecules to glioma.
glioma-derived factors can alter microglia functions in a way that promotes tumor growth.
the molecular profile of glioma-associated microglia is a complex and dynamic process that can be exploited in the design of novel cell-based therapies of glioma.

microglia can have a positive or negative effect on glioma progression depending on the stage of tumor growth.
